rationale: A legitimate complementarity test of two separately-validated archive legs, but it is combinatorial rather than new economics, and it stacks a third rank onto a moderator (net debt/assets) that already collapsed the cross-sectional slope to 1.52 in `harvest_that_accrues_to_equity` — likely a non-monotone, low-leverage/cash-holdings style tilt that industry-demeaning the other two legs cannot repair.

This is a single-operator ablation of an existing archive signal (adding IND_ADJ to the net-debt leg only) rather than a substantively different construction; the attribution question it poses is worth answering, but the answer is largely predictable — capital structure is heavily industry-determined, so demeaning will mostly strip the sector tilt and leave a weaker, mechanically similar version of a signal whose FMB slope was already insignificant.

The moderator RATIO(xint, ebitda) is sign-unstable — for negative or near-zero EBITDA the ratio flips negative and NEG() then assigns the *highest* rank to exactly the distressed firms the hypothesis wants to exclude, so the expression's natural direction contradicts the stated mechanism; interest coverage is also a well-worn distress/leverage proxy rather than a novel claimholder measure.

Wrapping one IND_ADJ around the capex leg of `capex_shortfall_given_a_windfall` is a cosmetic variant, not a new mechanism, and it introduces a subtle inconsistency the reasoning misses: after industry demeaning, the zero assigned to non-windfall firms is no longer the centre of the conditional distribution, so masked firms will systematically drift into one tail in industries with above- or below-average capex deviations.

NEG((Δceq − ib)/at) is the clean-surplus net payout / net equity issuance measure — a direct rediscovery of the well-documented net-issuance and net-payout-yield anomalies (Daniel–Titman, Pontiff–Woodgate, Boudoukh et al.) — and the reasoning's claim that it is "not a financing-anomaly proxy" is exactly backwards; it will also be contaminated by write-offs, dividends-in-kind and other clean-surplus violations.

A coherent, parsimonious two-leg combination of two independently validated modifications (durability on the profitability leg, peer-demeaning on both), with a well-posed question about whether sector purity survives when the windfall is measured as a persistent rather than transitory improvement — though it remains an incremental recombination rather than a new mechanism, and IND_ADJ of an already own-norm-demeaned quantity risks double-differencing away most of the surviving variation.
